finding.claim: The /users endpoint takes the org identifier from a client-supplied query parameter. The file has no authentication or authorization check tying the caller to that org, so any caller can list the users of any org (IDOR / broken access control). This depends on no auth middleware being mounted outside this file. The file shows none, and req.pg is also injected from outside it.
finding.sink: req.pg.query SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1, with results returned via res.json

trace.note: Route handler registered with no auth middleware
Attacker-controlled req.query.org is used directly as the org filter; it is not compared to any session or user org
Matching rows are returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: The query is parameterized ($1), so there is no SQL injection. I found no authentication, session, or org-membership check in the file. app.use is never called, so no middleware is registered here. Middleware outside this file could not be inspected.

verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (db.js:8-10 reads req.query.org, queries with it, and returns the rows, with no auth check and no app.use), but db.js:9 needs req.pg, which nothing in this directory sets. The directory holds only db.js, so I can't tell whether a deployment injects both req.pg and any auth from outside, and I can't confirm the endpoint is reachable and unprotected.
